name: Halberdiers
headerMeta: Silver era · Pike/Polearm infantry · anti-cav · 165 leadership · Honor Tree

origin.text: Silver-era unit unlocked in the infantry honor tree - already strong in its base form, unlike most promotion units. Picks up movement speed and damage upgrades in the unit tree, worth spending spare honor on.
unlock: Promotable to Landsknechts via Season 6 challenges

pitch: A cost-effective anti-cavalry pike unit and top-rated warband filler that deals far more damage in phalanx than most players realize, dominating once braced. It cannot solo-hold a line and folds to shielded units or a mid-formation overwhelm, so it needs a screening partner and careful micro to stay effective.

doctrines.name: Anti-Cavalry Doctrine V
doctrines.effect: -40% DMG taken from cavalry while bracing, +16% DMG vs cavalry while bracing.
doctrines.note: −35% DMG taken from cavalry while bracing, +DMG vs cavalry while bracing

doctrines.name: Anti-Cavalry Brace Doctrine
doctrines.effect: -30% DMG taken from cavalry when using Brace-type skills. Mandatory per OP.
doctrines.note: −30% DMG taken from cavalry when using brace-type skills

doctrines.name: Epic Bloodthirsty Doctrine
doctrines.effect: 12% lifesteal for 6s after dealing damage, +12% DMG when HP above 60%.

doctrines.name: Stun-on-brace doctrine
doctrines.note: Halberdier Sergeants get this from veterancy instead and can skip it

doctrines.name: Bleeding Brace Doctrine
doctrines.effect: Bracing inflicts bleeding on enemy cavalry: 16% max HP + 400 DMG. Filler.
doctrines.note: bracing inflicts bleeding on cavalry: 16% max HP + 400 DMG

doctrines.name: Pike Defence Doctrine
doctrines.note: strong vs high-tier cavalry, less needed in silver-only matchups — reduces DMG vs Outriders specifically

doctrines.name: Epic Piercing Damage Doctrine
doctrines.note: held in the last slot until the seasonal Pike Defense slot unlocks; base Piercing Penetration itself not recommended since penetration is already high

doctrines.name: "Bonus damage while bracing" doctrine
doctrines.effect: +100 dmg while bracing, affects Advance. Top pick.
doctrines.note: doesn't currently function in phalanx formation

veterancy.label: Bottom line
veterancy.body: Improves bracing — the unit spends most combat time braced, making this the primary choice.

veterancy.label: Top line
veterancy.body: Improves the charge ability, which has low damage and limited tactical value.

battleRole.positioning: Pair Halberdiers with another unit that screens them from flanks — they cannot solo-hold a line. {2} Each model can only hit two enemies at once, so being overwhelmed by too many targets at once gets them overrun. {2} Stay behind cover when possible and avoid frontal charges from shielded units.
battleRole.formation: Default F2 (phalanx/block): sustained damage and attack speed far exceed loose formation; formation issues can be largely avoided with correct positioning. {2} Requires all unit models to be at the X-move position to form properly, and if overwhelmed mid-formation the unit stops fighting to fix positions. {2} F1 (loose) trades that for burst impact damage vs charging cavalry, but is vulnerable to CC and weak if the initial burst doesn't kill. {2} Halberdier Sergeants (a related unit, same core logic) form up in F1 more easily and are tankier, performing somewhat better solo. {2}
battleRole.tips: Braced Halberdiers automatically face nearby enemies, reducing the need to worry about flanking or hero dives on artillery/ranged allies. {2} Charge ability should only be used from F1 with immediate post-hit brace; attempting it from phalanx makes the unit try to re-form mid-fight among enemies, which gets them killed. {2} If caught off-guard mid-formation, pressing V (defensive-stance cancel) can beat bracing in a bad position. {2} Experimental: while braced in phalanx, C then Space breaches to loose formation while keeping the phalanx damage bonus — reported untested in live play. {2}

cards.name: Imperial Spear Guard
cards.why: advance order is a safe frontal knockdown that directly counters brace-type skills; reserved for high-damage pikemen like Halberdiers

cards.name: shielded units
cards.why: weak block-break makes these a problem, and their frontal charge should be avoided rather than traded head-on

cards.name: Rattan Roundshields
cards.why: Halberdier charge ("bill-hooking"), if allowed to activate, flattens Roundshields outright

cards.name: Berserkers
cards.why: blue-tier Halberdiers using the C+Space phalanx-to-loose breach trick were able to kill Berserkers, something other formations couldn't manage

matchups.siblings: Halberdier Sergeants play the same way but skip the stun-on-brace doctrine since they get it from veterancy, form up in F1 more easily, and are tankier - so they hold up somewhat better solo. {2}

controls.notes: Core formation micro: move from F2 to F2 during the fight and let it brace — requires all models at X-move position to form properly. {1} If F2-to-F2 is too hard or the fight moves too fast, swap to F1 and insta-brace. {1} Formation "cheese": charge into a corner aiming upward to slide models into a dense stack, then F1 to orient and brace — press X and re-brace if a few models don't lock in; creator has never found a practical use for it. {2}
